§5.10 Slide Furniture

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-slide-furniture · rule layout slides

✅ Normative

Every printed navigation tab of a slide MUST be transcribed, in printed order, as furniture, and a highlight that identifies the active section MUST be kept with the highlight convention. Labels printed on a photograph MUST be kept with the photograph's description; purely decorative background art MUST NOT be described.

Presentation decks print things around their content that a document does not: a row of section tabs along the top edge with the current one highlighted, name labels overlaid on photographs, a running footer with the deck name and slide number.

Requirements

The slide prints The output
A row of navigation tabs Every tab, in printed order, as furniture; the active tab's highlight as <mark style="background-color: …"> with the nearest HTML colour name — see Highlighted Text§7.2.5
A label printed on a photograph The label, kept with the photograph's description
Background art with no labels, values or meaningful relationships Nothing
Background art whose geography or shape conveys content A description of what it conveys

✅ Sample — tabs, tiles and labelled photos

Three tabs top-left, the third filled red; a slide title and subtitle; four bullets and a stat-tile panel in the left card; two photographs, grey silhouettes each with a boxed name label at the lower right; a footnote; a footer with the slide number, deck name and a wordmark with a small symbol. The tabs are one furniture block in printed order, the active one highlighted; each photo becomes a one-line description carrying its label.
